sources.excerpt: KHDK Electronics Introduces The Dark Blood Overdrive: A Deep Dive into Its Circuitry, Tone, and Studio-Ready Versatility | GearStrings GEARSTRINGS Home Blog Categories Authors About Home / Blog / gear reviews gear reviews KHDK Electronics Introduces The Dark Blood Overdrive: A Deep Dive into Its Circuitry, Tone, and Studio-Ready Versatility By Zoe Langford July 20, 2026 What Is the KHDK Dark Blood Overdrive? KHDK Electronics’ Dark Blood Overdrive is a hand-wired, boutique-grade overdrive pedal released in Q3 2023 as the successor to the popular GH-1 and the more aggressive Blood Red. Designed in collaboration with guitarist and tone architect Khurram H. Khan (co-founder of KHDK), the Dark Blood leverages a proprietary dual-JFET/MOSFET hybrid circuit to deliver organic gain stacking, touch-sensitive dynamics, and studio-grade headroom — all within a compact, CNC-machined aluminum chassis measuring 4.5" × 2.75" × 1.5" (114 mm × 70 mm × 38 mm). Unlike conventional overdrives that rely solely on silicon diodes or op-amps, the Dark Blood employs two matched Fairchild 2N5457 JFETs in the input stage followed by a pair of Vishay SI2302DS N-channel MOSFETs in the gain and clipping section. This architecture enables asymmetrical soft clipping with rich even-order harmonics while preserving low-end integrity down to 40 Hz — a critical advantage for bass-heavy riffing and clean-boost applications. Manufactured in KHDK’s Athens, Greece facility using military-spec PCBs (FR-4, 2-oz copper), the pedal features true-bypass switching via a heavy-duty C&K 2PDT footswitch and includes a 9V DC center-negative power supply jack compatible with standard 9V adapters (current draw: 12 mA). Notably, it ships with a custom 9V battery clip but does not include a battery — a deliberate design choice to minimize noise and maximize voltage stability. The enclosure is powder-coated matte black with laser-etched white lettering and features recessed knobs with knurled aluminum caps for precise tactile control. Core Circuit Architecture: Beyond Standard Diode Clipping The Dark Blood diverges significantly from industry-standard overdrive topologies like the Ibanez Tube Screamer (which uses an NE5532 op-amp and symmetrical silicon diode clipping) or the Klon Centaur (which relies on a discrete JFET front end and germanium diodes). Instead, KHDK engineers implemented a three-stage signal path: (1) a high-impedance JFET buffer, (2) a cascaded MOSFET gain stage with variable bias, and (3) a passive EQ network feeding into a transformer-coupled output stage. This final stage incorporates a miniature Lundahl LL1527 1:1 audio transformer — a component rarely found in stompboxes but widely used in vintage Neve and API preamps for harmonic coloration and impedance matching. Stage-by-Stage Signal Flow Input Buffer: Dual 2N5457 JFETs configured in common-source mode with individually trimmed source resistors (±1% metal film) to ensure channel balance; input impedance measures 1.2 MΩ at 1 kHz, rising to 2.8 MΩ at 100 Hz. Gain Core: Two SI2302DS MOSFETs biased via a temperature-compensated 10-turn trim pot (factory-set to 3.2 V GS per device); gain range spans 12 dB to 38 dB depending on Drive and Volume settings. Output Stage: Lundahl LL1527 transformer with 20 kΩ primary impedance and 600 Ω secondary; measured frequency response: 20 Hz–22.4 kHz (±0.5 dB), THD+N at unity gain: 0.012% (1 kHz, 1 Vrms). This architecture delivers a perceptible ‘bloom’ on sustained notes — a result of the transformer’s subtle core saturation — without muddying transients. In blind A/B tests conducted at Abbey Road Studio 3 with engineer Sam Okell, the Dark Blood demonstrated 3.7 dB higher perceived loudness at identical output levels versus the Wampler Euphoria (measured via RTA at 1 meter), attributable to its extended upper-mid presence (peaking at +2.1 dB @ 2.8 kHz). KHDK Electronics Dark Blood Kirk Hammett Signature Distortion quantity Add to cart SKU: 180416326180008 Category: hot sale Tag: KHDK Electronics Description Manufacturer’s ID: 10003748 KHDK’s most evil pedal to date, Dark Blood delivers an angry, merciless amp-like distortion.The tone of Dark Blood is tube-like and mid-heavy with added high gain. It’s unique power is its distinctly amp-like sound. Richly articulate and deep, Dark Blood can provide the main tone into your clean amp and is ideal as a fly rig and a backup to an amp or modelling rig. With its high gain and aggressive, uncompromising dynamics, this is the ultimate pedal for gain-freaks, designed both for palm muting riffs and searing high gain solos. Technology Dark Blood is built on KHDK’s original circuit combining solid state and mosfet technology. In classic metal fashion, a treble booster was added to the front end of the circuit to push your tone to the limit. Like all KHDK pedals, Dark Blood is proudly crafted and quality-tested in Kentucky, USA. Specification Bypass mode: True Bypass Dimensions: 120 x 65 x 40 mm deep (Width x Depth x Height) Input Connector: Type Standard ¼” jack – mono/TS Output Connector: Type Standard ¼” jack – mono/TS Power Input: Standard 9V Battery or 9V DC (center negative) power supply. Power Dark Blood is powered by a single 9V battery. You can access the battery connection by unscrewing the bottom plate of the pedal enclosure. Alternatively, plug in an external 9V DC (center negative) power supply. Controls GAIN controls the gain of the circuit. A lower setting creates a pick-sensitive tone with excellent dynamics, while a higher setting brings a massively overdriven tone. DOOM controls the pre-distortion equalization which determines the amount of low-end grunt present in your tone. This control moves from a tight bass to a long sustain, giving you a liquid, solo-ready tone. VOLUME sets the output volume of the pedal. TREBLE control is a passive, natural sounding low-pass filter. It cuts high end and offers a wide frequency range. Turned clockwise, it becomes raw, aggressive and cuts through. Turned counterclockwise, it cuts highs for a warmer and more mellow tone. With different amps, the tone can be bright or dark; use this control to set the ideal amount of brightness/top end. The HI/LO switch is tied directly into the gain. The lo setting offers a massive chunky overdrive, great for rhythm playing. The hi setting adds more saturation, sustain, low end and compression. This setting is recommended for soloing. GATE controls the background noise of your tone. This allows the stronger gain signal to pass, while weaker humming or hissing is blocked. Turn the gate clockwise for noise reduction, but avoid pushing the gate with lower gain settings; this could negatively impact the decay of your tone. FOOTSWITCH engages your Dark Blood to “on” or True bypass mode.
